solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See group developed self-critical conscience

indicators.note: developed suggests something worked up into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to look at a group whose members have grown a self-critical conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of SEE GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: In Freudian psychology the superego is the part of the mind acting as a moral, self-judging conscience.

clue.text: Maintain one putting money aside must suffer initial small loss

indicators.note: the opening letter, an S for small, is lost from the front of the word

parts.note: someone who puts money aside is a saver

explanation.surface: A thrifty person keeping up the habit, though suffering a small loss at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must suffer initial small loss' takes S (small) off the front of SAVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or affirm firmly, which is one sense of maintaining something is true.

clue.text: Text rules announcing what could reduce the wages of sin?

indicators.note: announcing means the phrase is spoken, so the entry is what it sounds like

parts.words: what could reduce the wages of sin
parts.note: a tax on sin would cut its rewards: a sin tax, playing on the biblical 'the wages of sin is death'

explanation.surface: A rulebook for text that proclaims a way to cut what sin pays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'announcing' signals a sound-alike: SIN TAX is said like the answer. 'The wages of sin' echoes Romans 6:23.
explanation.definitionFit: Syntax is the set of grammatical rules governing how words are arranged into sentences.

clue.text: Rubbish about litre being a very generous measure of spirits

definitions.text: a very generous measure of spirits

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: tripe is nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: Talk of a litre being a generous pour of spirits is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L (litre) inside TRIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A triple is a pub measure of spirits three times the standard single, so very generous.

clue.text: Respectful at all times during split

indicators.note: during means one word sits within the span of the other

parts.note: rent is a past tense of rend, meaning torn or split
ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: Someone stays respectful throughout, even during a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' is a past participle here: torn, as in rend, rent, rent. 'during' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Reverent describes showing deep respect or veneration, a close synonym.

clue.text: Host is extremely foolish going topless

indicators.note: losing its top means the word's first letter is removed in this down clue

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad or extremely foolish

explanation.surface: A host who goes topless is seen as extremely foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' drops the B from BARMY.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a multitude or army, as in the biblical heavenly host.

clue.text: Voyeurs going round — right? One checking out a house?

indicators.note: going round suggests the letters circulate into a new order

explanation.surface: Peeping toms doing the rounds of a house, and is that acceptable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' is the anagram signal, not a circling move; the question mark marks the definition as playful, since a surveyor does check out houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A surveyor inspects a property's condition, typically before a house purchase.

clue.text: Old regret backing common currency

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Lingering regret about going back to the shared European money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns O + RUE around.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the single currency shared by many European Union states.

clue.text: Wager about one game in Mediterranean capital

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the others

parts.note: a bet is a wager
I is the Roman numeral one
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Betting on a game in a Mediterranean capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the insertion; RU for rugby union is a standard crossword abbreviation for 'game'.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut, the capital of Lebanon, lies on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Prays in eastern temple yard, initially displaying this?

definitions.text: Prays in eastern temple yard, initially displaying this?

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: Someone praying in the courtyard of an eastern temple, showing devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of Prays In Eastern Temple Yard, while the whole clue describes the quality shown.
explanation.definitionFit: Piety is religious devotion, the very thing displayed by praying in a temple.

clue.text: Area by lake left for everybody

explanation.surface: An area beside a lake set aside for everyone's use.
explanation.definitionFit: All, used as a pronoun, means every person, everyone.

clue.text: Summit held in Dover, Texas

indicators.note: held in means the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A summit meeting staged in a small town called Dover, Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' points to the letters inside doVER TEXas.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertex is the highest point or apex, a peak or summit.

clue.text: The old Republican is beginning to trust no practical person?

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: An old Republican who is starting to put no faith in anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes the T of trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorist deals in ideas rather than practice, so is not a practical person, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Free English parliamentarian trapped in extension

indicators.note: trapped in means the next pieces are enclosed inside the other word

parts.note: EXT is the abbreviation for a telephone extension
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An English MP stuck in an office extension wants to be set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped in' signals the insertion; 'Free' is a verb here, to release, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt is to release someone from an obligation, so to free them.

clue.text: Set school work read badly

parts.note: prep is British boarding-school slang for homework

indicators.note: badly means the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A pupil's assigned homework, read out poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal for 'read', giving ARED; 'Set' is the adjective, as in 'all set'.
explanation.definitionFit: Set can mean ready, as in 'all set', which is a synonym of prepared.

clue.text: Stick together with Commanding Officer present

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Troops keep together when their commanding officer is present.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold firmly together, to be united.

clue.text: Abstain from school in little rising

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the other
rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little

explanation.surface: Keeping away from school while still a little child growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the Scots word for little, since a down answer reads upward; 'in' then signals the school abbreviation going inside, giving EEW split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew is to deliberately avoid or shun, as one abstains from something.

clue.text: Learnt to play horn

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters are moved about freely into another order

explanation.surface: Someone has learned to play the horn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to play' rearranges LEARNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An antler is the branched bony horn of a deer.

clue.text: Cold in truck in the far north

indicators.note: in means the first piece is placed inside the second

parts.note: an artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck

explanation.surface: Feeling cold in a truck cab up in the far north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside ARTIC, British slang for an articulated lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic describes the polar region around the North Pole, so it means located in the far north.

clue.text: Second rook capturing one knight

indicators.note: capturing means the outer pieces take in and hold the inner one

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A chess move in which a second rook takes a piece, perhaps the knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' puts I between S and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the title given to a knight.

clue.text: Player pitch regularly dropped in song

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped from these words, so the alternate remaining ones are kept

explanation.surface: A performer's pitch keeps falling during a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly dropped' removes P, A, E, P, T, H from PLAYER PITCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem or the words of a song, so loosely a song.

clue.text: Art-song survived with verse missing

indicators.note: missing means the letter named is left out of the word

parts.note: lived means survived

explanation.surface: An art-song that lasted through the ages even without one of its verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes V (verse) out of LIVED.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art-song of the Romantic era, such as those by Schubert.

clue.text: Contemporary black fuel containing derv regularly

indicators.note: containing means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: coal is a black fuel

indicators.note: regularly means alternate letters are taken from the word

explanation.surface: Modern black fuel blended with diesel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes E and V from DERV, British for diesel; 'containing' puts them inside COAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A coeval is someone of the same age or era, a contemporary.

clue.text: Child's toy losing head in circular movement

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a teddy bear is a child's toy

explanation.surface: A child's toy loses its head while spinning round in circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the T of TEDDY.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a swirling, circular current of water or air.

clue.text: Pickle or jam in army dining room

definitions.meaning: a jam is a tight spot

explanation.surface: Pickle or jam served at an army dining hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Mess means both a difficult fix and the room where soldiers or officers eat.

clue.text: Unusual red olive is a really bad one

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are made odd, turned into another order

explanation.surface: An odd red olive is truly rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges RED OLIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An evildoer is a wicked person, someone truly bad.
